summary: Historical upgrade review: OMP import resume (#1612), lazy message estimates (#1531), typed end reasons (#1334), and harness inventory (#1516); unblock daily publication without changing runtime code

replay.detail: None of these four first-parent changes adds a startup graph replay, schema-version migration, or replay trigger. #1531 moves the existing agent-message estimate cache backfill from store open to the first estimate request; that derived-cache rebuild is not a full claim replay. That request waits for an atomic rebuild, while an already-pinned read snapshot folds its retained sends without writing. #1612 reads existing native bindings and canonical claim order; #1334 projects terminal evidence at the requested snapshot; #1516 publishes new inventory observations. Neither the retention-policy change nor the new claim fields alone proves replay.

schema.detail: #1531 changes initialization and maintenance of existing local agent_message_sends/day-counter cache state and its agent_message_days_v1 readiness marker: sends update coordination before initialization, and the first estimate transaction rebuilds counters from retained sends. It adds no table, index, trigger, or numeric schema transition. #1612 adds the optional desired_token field to harness.session-file claim/resource validation, not SQLite DDL. #1334 changes read projections and snapshot queries only. #1516 adds the harness.inventory.observed claim kind and latest-observation publication using existing storage, not new SQLite objects. No database-version downgrade or forward-only DDL migration is introduced by these four changes.

rules.detail: None of these four changes alters the checkpoint rules digest or numeric RULES_VERSION. #1516 adds harness.inventory.observed to the retention policy's kinds table as current/on-change with a pending reader audit, but adds no checkpoint rule. Policy::rules_description() serializes described rules only, not kinds; the checkpoint engine description and RULES_VERSION are also unchanged. This introduces no additional coordinated checkpoint upgrade requirement. #1612 changes OMP continuation/refusal precedence to canonical claim order, independently of checkpoint sealing.

compatibility.detail: #1612 introduces launcher-owned ST3_LAUNCH_DESIRED_TOKEN and optional desired_token in native-session reports/bindings. Imported OMP seats bootstrap with validated ST3_NATIVE_RESUME_SESSION/PATH rather than authored resume arguments, then continue their incarnation-bound managed session; missing/mismatched transcripts fail closed. Use matching launcher/driver behavior; an older binding lacking provenance is not proof that the import bootstrap completed. #1531 preserves the usage response shape but the first estimate may be slower. #1334 adds optional end_reason to agent resources and Rust/Swift/TypeScript models; clients must tolerate its absence and must not infer completion from missing exit evidence. #1516 adds fenced harness-inventory reads, a signed peer-read operation, inventory-unavailable errors, and OMP command observations from the managed channel. Older servers/peers do not implement these additions; skills remain unsupported and command inventory is explicitly partial. Exact old/new client, peer, and OMP version pairs were not exercised for this historical review; deploy matching builds for the new functionality rather than assuming cross-version support.

downtime.detail: No change here forces a fleet restart or introduces measured restart-to-API/restart-to-health timings; use the standard scheduled service restart to activate new binaries. #1531 removes the estimate backfill from startup, but its first non-snapshot usage request performs an atomic writer transaction whose duration and contention depend on retained sends and were not measured here; allow for a slow first estimate rather than assuming API recovery waits for it. #1612 can refuse an affected imported seat's launch until its exact transcript and selectors are valid. #1334 is a read-only projection change. #1516 can return unavailable/stale-fence for inventory while native binding is unconfirmed or evidence is inaccessible; this is not evidence of whole-service downtime.

manual.detail: #1612: preserve imported OMP transcript files and artifacts at their pinned absolute paths until bootstrap binds; remove conflicting authored session-selection flags and repair a refused import using the strict session/path handshake documented in docs/seat-lifecycle.md. Continuation after binding uses the managed session inventory; relocating a continuation outside that inventory is unsupported. Preserve identity and transcripts rather than starting a replacement session to hide a refusal, and verify the native session binding after restart. #1531 initializes estimates automatically with no operator cache migration. #1334 requires no store repair or manual lifecycle rewrite. #1516 requires a matching managed OMP producer and confirmed session/ready binding for inventory; callers must supply owner/session/incarnation fences and handle unsupported/unavailable collections. This backfill PR itself only adds release metadata; publication remains with the daily release automation.

recovery.detail: #1531 reuses the existing derived-cache format and #1334 only changes projections, so neither adds a forward-only database migration; this does not certify rollback across the rest of the release interval. #1612 adds durable binding fields and #1516 adds a claim kind, current/on-change observation storage, and peer/client operations that older builds may not understand. Old-build admission and swap-back after those observations were not verified. Preserve claim backups, local native transcripts/artifacts, and identity before upgrade; follow docs/upgrading-st.md and docs/st3/compatibility.md. Prefer a compatible roll-forward for binding/inventory failures; reinstalling an older binary does not remove new claims or relocate transcripts.
